messages:
ana: Quick heads-up — after the kernel-selector tweak (heuristic v3.2) I saw a sharp rise in OOMs on long-context inference jobs. p95 latency stable but memory footprint +~15% on our replay trace. Posting a short perf dump.

ana: perf snippet:
```
trace: run-2026-03-17
model: redwood-open-13b
kernel_selector: v3.2
batching: auto
workspace_alloc_target: 14GB -> 16GB
ooms_24h: 3 -> 12
avg_block_alloc: 1.2MB
block_reuse_hits: 42%
kv_cache_evictions: +18%
```

rui: This matches my earlier suspicion — fused-attn path in v3.2 allocates larger temporary workspaces per stream. BlockManager seems slow to return freed blocks into the slab pool, so fragmentation grows and we end up OOMing even though aggregate free bytes exist.

sam: Could be the repool logic. We recently gated eager repool behind `repool_enabled=false` for latency regressions. Can we try `repool_enabled=true` + smaller block size for a short canary?

jord: Agreed. I propose a canary config:
```
BLOCK_SIZE=32768           # 32KB (was 64KB)
REPOOL_ENABLED=true
SLAB_REPOOL_THRESHOLD=0.6  # allow returns when 60% free
WORKSPACE_TARGET=14GB
```

maria: Tradeoff to note: smaller blocks reduce internal fragmentation and make reuse faster, but increase bookkeeping and compaction frequency. Expect CPU compaction cost to rise — watch compaction-ms and cpu%.

ci-bot: Canary deploy queued for `eng-runtime/canary/1876549999` by @ana — https://ci.redwood.internal/build/3821 :rocket:

ana: Canary completed (2 hours). Summary: OOMs dropped from 12->1 on the long-context trace. p99 latency +2%, p95 unchanged. Compaction CPU increased ~12% but stayed within our emergency threshold. Block reuse hits improved from 42% -> 71%. KV cache evictions reduced by ~9%.

sam: Nice! Do we have memory heatmap snapshots?

ana: Uploaded two screenshots to the thread (link in workspace). Quick diffs: free-slab-chunks increased, large contiguous free extents appear more often with repool enabled.

jord: Given these results, next steps: revert the earlier kernel-selector change in prod until we can either 1) make repool the default with tuned thresholds, or 2) implement a lightweight workspace pooling layer in the fused kernel to avoid per-request big allocs.

maria: Also add a regression test: replay long-context batches with synthetic KV patterns and assert OOMs==0 and compaction-ms < 250ms.

ana: I'll open a PR with the canary config and the regression harness (WIP). Suggest block size middle-ground of 48KB for broader workloads.

sam: +1 to 48KB. Also add telemetry for `block_reuse_hits` and `slab_repool_ops` per-minute so we can watch it in Grafana.

rui: I'll look into a smaller follow-up: change kernel allocator path to request from a dedicated small-pool instead of calloc for fused-attn. Might remove the need for aggressive repool.

ana: Thanks all. Filed follow-ups: ENGRT-1289 (repool default toggle), ENGRT-1290 (kernel pool), ENGRT-1291 (regression test). :thumbsup:

maria: love it — great experiment and clear metrics.

ci-bot: PR opened: https://git.redwood.internal/p/eng-runtime/merge/1402 (WIP)
